description: A change told in order: the old state fills in, an arrow draws, the old state fades and the new one lights up.
useWhen: One thing changes over time: a refactor, a fix, a new process.

long.title: What changed in the deployment process after moving to a pipeline

before.label: Manual deployments
points: Someone copies the files to the server by hand on Friday
Every release depends on a long checklist in a shared doc
Rolling back means restoring last night's full backup
Bugs are found by users, usually a few hours later
Only two people in the team know how the whole thing works

after.label: Automated pipeline
points: Every merge is built, tested and released the same way
The checklist now lives in the repository, as reviewed code
Rolling back is a single click and takes under one minute
Bugs are caught by tests, before any user can ever see them
Anyone on the team can release, even on their very first day

captions: For two years, each release was a small ceremony.
Now releasing is so boring that nobody stops to look at it.
